summary: thumbs.py frames the projected silhouette to 70 % of the frame at 48 % height and adds an exposure floor: a 192 px probe render measures the mean luminance of the opaque part pixels and a bracketing search lifts dark parts (up to +2.5 EV) until it reaches 0.10 (2:1 against #23282E). All 48 renders re-rendered and re-encoded, filenames unchanged (D241). Placeholder-grade models (hauba, stakla) were not remodelled (not cheap).

summary: PMREM prefilter moved to the pipeline: 3d/scripts/env.mjs bakes three's cube-UV atlas (cube 64, RLE RGBE, 139 KB) and the runtime binds it with CubeUVReflectionMapping, so no PMREMGenerator or blur-shader compile runs at 3D start. Every material texture is uploaded with initTexture before compileAsync and the edge programs compile through compileAsync before their first frame (D243). docs/3d/WEB-QA.md section 4 updated.

summary: On teardown the canvas disposes three's module-level DFG LUT (found through the material uniforms); its 'dispose' listener kept every old renderer, its context and the detached home DOM alive. R3F 9.8.1 already calls gl.dispose() and forceContextLoss; scene.environment is cleared and the baked environment has no PMREM render target any more; heroStore.controller is already cleared by HeroStage on unmount (D244).

summary: msaaFor(tier, dpr): 4x MSAA only on the high tier below DPR 1.5; HeroCanvas uses it for the antialias context attribute. Contract F5 now states that the drawing buffer counts toward the 60 MB (D244).

summary: tier.ts reads the WebGL renderer string (WEBGL_debug_renderer_info) in its single probe context; SwiftShader, llvmpipe, softpipe and Microsoft Basic Render are classified low (posters). ?3d=high|mid still forces a tier for QA and e2e. No runtime frame watchdog: demand rendering cannot tell a slow frame from an idle gap (D244).
verification: AUDIT_BASE=http://localhost:3001 node scripts/qa/fix/hero-3d-assets-tier.mjs -> '(no override) dpr 1: {"tier":"low","status":"idle","canvas":false}' on SwiftShader and '?3d=high dpr 1: tier high, status ready'. Unit test 'software WebGL renderers are low (PERF-23)' passes.
